title: Plateaus
source: After the notes' South America physical maps, with standard UPSC facts added

places.name: Bolivian Plateau
places.significance: The high tableland of Lake Titicaca and La Paz, lying between the ranges of the Andes — the highest plateau outside Tibet
notes: An intermontane plateau — one enclosed by mountains

places.name: Mato Grosso Plateau
places.significance: Brazil's great central tableland, the divide between the rivers flowing north to the Amazon and south to the Paraná

places.name: Borborema Plateau
places.significance: The upland of Brazil's north-eastern bulge, whose seaward slope catches the rain the dry interior behind it lacks

places.name: Patagonian Plateau
places.significance: Stepped tableland east of the southern Andes in Argentina — a piedmont plateau, built up at the mountains' foot
notes: A piedmont plateau — one at the foot of mountains, as against an intermontane one enclosed by them
